ads_analysis.account_level_diagnosis: The account is primarily budget-constrained across the growth-driving campaigns: most campaigns sit at ~100% budget utilization with 73–83% impression share lost to budget and 0% lost to rank at the campaign level (e.g., Shopping - Apparel: 18% IS with 82% lost budget; Non-Brand Search - Seasonal Promo: 21% IS with 79% lost budget). However, within Search there is also a meaningful rank/efficiency layer to fix: several high-quality keywords are still losing the majority of impressions to rank (e.g., "winter jacket sale" QS 8.0 with 79% lost rank), while some low-QS queries consume spend at very high CPA (e.g., "deals near me today" QS 2.5, $152.52 spend, $762.6 cost/conv). Net: unlock incremental volume by reallocating/raising budgets where ROAS supports it, and tighten query/keyword controls to prevent wasted spend and rank drag.
notable_patterns: Five in-scope growth campaigns are effectively hard-capped by budget: Shopping - Apparel/Electronics/Home & Garden (99.9% budget utilization; 81–83% lost to budget; 17–19% IS), Non-Brand Search - Seasonal Promo (99.9% utilization; 79% lost budget; 21% IS), and Performance Max - Full Catalog (99.9% utilization; 81% lost budget; 19% IS).

Brand Search - US is not budget-capped (75.4% budget utilization) yet still shows 40% impression share lost to budget with 60% IS—suggesting budget pacing/allocation issues rather than pure demand exhaustion; it also delivers the best efficiency (ROAS 10.51 on $5,047.88).

Search query waste is materially tied to competitor brand “zero-click” exposure: 8,280 impressions on competitor terms (e.g., "metro retail co", "northfield mercantile", "union square goods"), with 51% of search-term impressions coming from zero-click competitor terms and only 0.2 conversions attributed to a competitor-like term ("fairmont retail quote").

Within Search, rank is a secondary constraint at the keyword level despite campaign-level ‘0% lost rank’: high-QS terms still lose most impressions to rank ("holiday electronics deals" QS 7.5 with 81% lost rank; "winter jacket sale" QS 8.0 with 79% lost rank; "pilot account promo code" QS 9.5 with 42% lost rank), indicating bid/eligibility or segmentation issues at the keyword/ad group layer.

campaign_findings.diagnosis: Very low reach (18% impression share) with 82% lost to budget and 99.9% budget utilization indicates the campaign is demand-rich but throttled. Current efficiency is weak (ROAS 1.45 on $5,491.96), so budget increases should be paired with feed/product-level tightening rather than a blind scale.
campaign_findings.recommended_action: Reallocate budget to the best-performing product groups and suppress low-margin/low-ROAS inventory before increasing the overall cap; then scale budget in steps while guarding ROAS.

campaign_findings.diagnosis: Reach is similarly constrained (17% IS; 83% lost to budget; 99.9% utilization). With ROAS 1.42 on $3,550.60, the immediate opportunity is not just more budget, but budget + better assortment/bidding control so incremental spend doesn’t dilute returns.
campaign_findings.recommended_action: Tighten product targeting (exclude/segment poor performers) and only then raise budget to capture the 83% budget-lost impression share.

campaign_findings.diagnosis: Large missed volume (19% IS; 81% lost to budget; 99.9% utilization) with comparatively better ROAS (1.88 on $3,896.20) than other Shopping categories suggests this is the best Shopping candidate to fund first.
campaign_findings.recommended_action: Prioritize incremental budget here ahead of other Shopping campaigns, scaling until marginal ROAS approaches your floor; keep the rest constrained until efficiency work is done.

campaign_findings.diagnosis: Campaign is hard-capped (21% IS; 79% lost to budget; 99.9% utilization) while maintaining strong average quality (avg QS 8.8). But wasted spend signals exist in low-QS, high-CPA keywords (e.g., "deals near me today" QS 2.5, $762.6 cost/conv) and competitor-brand query leakage (8,280 impressions; 51% of impressions from zero-click competitor terms).
campaign_findings.recommended_action: Cut waste (competitor-brand negatives; pause/limit worst QS/CPA terms; fix negative conflicts) to free budget, then increase budget to capture incremental non-brand demand profitably.

campaign_findings.diagnosis: Capped by budget (19% IS; 81% lost budget; 99.9% utilization) with moderate efficiency (ROAS 2.15 on $994.03). It likely competes for the same catalog demand as Shopping; scaling should follow Shopping clean-up and query control to avoid cannibalization and low-quality expansion.
campaign_findings.recommended_action: Hold or modestly increase budget only after Shopping/product segmentation improvements; ensure it’s not funding the same low-return inventory you’re trying to constrain elsewhere.

recommendation_cards.title: Stop competitor-brand leakage that’s soaking impressions with near-zero conversions
recommendation_cards.what_data_shows: Search terms show 8,280 impressions on competitor-brand queries (e.g., "metro retail co", "northfield mercantile", "union square goods"), and 51% of search-term impressions are from zero-click competitor terms. Only 0.2 conversions appear on a competitor-like term ("fairmont retail quote"), indicating very weak payoff relative to impression volume.
recommended_steps: Add competitor brand names (and close variants) as negatives in the non-brand Search campaign(s) and any catch-all targeting that can match them.
Split a small, explicitly budget-capped competitor campaign only if conquesting is a strategic requirement; otherwise exclude entirely.
Re-check search-term routing after 3–5 days to confirm competitor terms drop materially while core promo/category terms remain eligible.
recommendation_cards.what_to_watch: Share of impressions from competitor-brand terms moving from 51% toward <10%, while non-brand conversions and CPA remain stable or improve.

recommendation_cards.title: Fix negative-keyword conflicts that are blocking your own demand in Seasonal Promo
recommendation_cards.what_data_shows: The negative-keyword conflicts report shows 3 conflicts causing an estimated 6,940 blocked impressions in Non-Brand Search - Seasonal Promo, including "free" blocking "free shipping promo code" (5,200 blocked impressions), "DIY" blocking "kitchen appliances clearance DIY install" (980), and "returns" blocking "winter jacket sale returns policy" (760).
recommended_steps: Change the conflicting negatives to narrower match/placement (e.g., apply at the right scope) so they stop blocking the intended keywords, or carve the affected keywords into their own ad group/campaign with tailored negatives.
If the intent is undesirable (e.g., ‘free’ seekers), then pause the blocked keyword instead—don’t rely on a negative that also blocks planned coverage.
After changes, validate impression lift specifically on the three blocked keyword themes while monitoring conversion rate.
recommendation_cards.what_to_watch: Impressions on the affected keyword themes increasing by ~6k+ per quarter run-rate (directionally), without a drop in conversion rate.

recommendation_cards.title: Reallocate budget to the best marginal return before raising overall caps
recommendation_cards.what_data_shows: Multiple campaigns are maxed out (99.9% budget utilization) and losing 79–83% impression share to budget: Shopping - Apparel (82%), Electronics (83%), Home & Garden (81%), Non-Brand Seasonal Promo (79%), and Performance Max (81%). Among Shopping categories, Home & Garden has the strongest ROAS (1.88) vs Apparel (1.45) and Electronics (1.42), suggesting better marginal efficiency if funded first.
recommended_steps: Shift incremental daily budget first into Shopping - Home & Garden (ROAS 1.88) and Performance Max (ROAS 2.15) if it is incrementally profitable, while keeping Apparel/Electronics constrained until product-level clean-up is done.
Use a staged approach (e.g., +10–20% budget changes) and reassess marginal ROAS/CPA after each step rather than doubling caps.
If total budget is fixed, fund these increases by reducing spend on the identified low-CPA-efficiency keywords/queries (see next card) and on competitor-brand leakage.
recommendation_cards.what_to_watch: Budget lost impression share in the funded campaigns falling (e.g., Home & Garden from 81% toward <60%) while ROAS holds within an acceptable band.

recommendation_cards.title: Cut/contain the worst low-QS, high-CPA keywords to free budget for capped campaigns
recommendation_cards.what_data_shows: Several low-quality, high-spend keywords show extreme cost per conversion: "deals near me today" (QS 2.5) spent $152.52 at $762.6 cost/conv; "kitchen appliances clearance" (QS 3.0) spent $97.52 at $325.07 cost/conv; "free shipping promo code" (QS 3.5) spent $250.38 at $139.1 cost/conv (and is simultaneously entangled in a negative conflict elsewhere).
recommended_steps: Pause or sharply reduce bids on the worst offender ("deals near me today") and review the search terms it matched to add intent negatives (e.g., local ‘near me’ modifiers if you don’t support local shopping).
Move remaining low-QS but strategically important terms into tightly themed ad groups with tailored ads/landing pages to raise relevance, or cap them with low bids and strict match types.
Reinvest the freed spend into budget-capped, higher-intent areas (Seasonal Promo core terms; best Shopping category) once waste is reduced.
recommendation_cards.what_to_watch: Cost/conv on these terms improving materially (e.g., $762.6 trending down by >50%) and overall budget lost IS decreasing in the campaigns you re-fund.

recommendation_cards.title: Address keyword-level rank loss on high-QS terms with controlled bid and structure tweaks
recommendation_cards.what_data_shows: Despite strong quality, key seasonal terms are losing impression share to rank at the keyword level: "holiday electronics deals" (QS 7.5; 19% IS; 81% lost rank) and "winter jacket sale" (QS 8.0; 21% IS; 79% lost rank). Even "pilot account promo code" has QS 9.5 but 42% lost rank, indicating missed visibility on high-intent brand+promo queries.
recommended_steps: Isolate these high-intent terms into dedicated ad groups with the tightest possible keyword-to-ad alignment and landing page mapping, then apply modest bid increases to test rank recovery.
Use query-level negatives to prevent these ad groups from absorbing broad/low-intent traffic while you bid up for rank.
Evaluate impression share lost to rank and top-of-page rate after changes; keep only the bid increases that pay back in CPA/ROAS.
recommendation_cards.what_to_watch: Impression share lost to rank on these terms dropping (e.g., from ~80% toward <50%) while maintaining acceptable CPA/ROAS.

already_working: Ad creation is not a bottleneck: 100% of ads are rated Good or Excellent (4 Excellent, 4 Good).

Auction position vs competitors is broadly competitive (avg outranking share 52.9% and top-of-page rate self 49.6% vs competitor avg 42.4%), so the biggest limiter is not head-to-head positioning—it's budget caps and query waste.
Brand Search - US is highly efficient (ROAS 10.51 on $5,047.88), so scaling should prioritize protecting brand coverage while you clean up non-brand and Shopping efficiency first.

market_mapping.why_now_summary: Retail search competition and spend are rising in the pilot’s core market, while the account is currently hard-capped by budget in multiple growth campaigns (losing ~79–83% of impression share to budget). At the same time, competitor brands are materially present (with sizable spend shares and active creative volumes), and query demand for at least one of the account’s key seasonal terms is up. Acting now to (1) stop competitor-term leakage and negative conflicts, and (2) reallocate/raise budgets where marginal returns can support it, is urgent because the market is getting more expensive/competitive as demand increases—so every week of being budget-throttled and wasting impressions on competitor terms leaves incremental, high-intent volume on the table.

supporting_facts.fact: United States (pilot account market) shows "Search Spend Growth QoQ" of 9.0% and "Vertical-Avg Impression Share" of 35.0%.
supporting_facts.relevance_to_recommendation: Supports urgency to address budget caps now: if search spend is growing 9.0% QoQ in the US, competitive pressure is rising. Remaining budget-constrained (and losing the majority of IS to budget) risks falling further behind as auctions heat up; resolving waste + reallocating/raising budgets protects share while the market accelerates.

supporting_facts.fact: Retail (Highlighted Market: United States) shows "Spend Growth QoQ" of 9.0% and "Query Demand Growth QoQ" of 6.0%, with "Vertical-Avg Impression Share" at 35.0%.
supporting_facts.relevance_to_recommendation: Directly aligns with the diagnosis: demand (+6.0% QoQ) and spend (+9.0% QoQ) are increasing in Retail US, so being capped (and inefficiently allocating spend) has an immediate opportunity cost. Also implies there is headroom vs a 35.0% vertical-average IS when the account’s cited campaign IS levels are far lower (e.g., 17–21%).

supporting_facts.fact: Metro Retail Co holds 28% "Spend Share" with 64 "Active Creatives" and runs on "Search, Social, Video".
supporting_facts.relevance_to_recommendation: Strengthens the case to stop competitor leakage and protect/expand coverage: a major competitor allocates a large spend share (28%) and is active in Search—meaning competitor presence on the SERP is likely persistent. If the account is leaking impressions into competitor queries with near-zero conversions, that waste is more damaging in a heavily funded competitive set.

supporting_facts.fact: Northfield Mercantile holds 21% "Spend Share" with 51 "Active Creatives" and runs on "Search, Social".
supporting_facts.relevance_to_recommendation: Reinforces that multiple competitors are investing heavily in Search; the account’s budget caps (and any misallocation to low-intent competitor terms) will more quickly translate into lost visibility on core non-brand/category demand. Supports urgency for negative keyword hygiene and budget reallocation toward highest-return campaigns/products.

supporting_facts.fact: Fairmont Outfitters holds 13% "Spend Share" with 33 "Active Creatives" and runs on "Search, Video".
supporting_facts.relevance_to_recommendation: Adds evidence that competitor brands (which the account is already matching into) are meaningfully funded in Search. This increases the urgency to either exclude competitor brands (if conquesting isn’t strategic) or isolate them into a tightly capped conquest campaign so capped growth campaigns don’t subsidize low-return competitor traffic.

supporting_facts.fact: The keyword "winter jacket sale" index moves from 100 (Q4 2025) to 121 (Q3 2026), showing 21% growth.
supporting_facts.relevance_to_recommendation: Directly supports acting now on the account’s keyword-level rank loss and budget constraints on seasonal search: one of the exact keywords flagged in the diagnosis is showing +21% growth, so fixing rank/eligibility (and ensuring budgets aren’t throttling the associated campaign/ad group) is time-sensitive to capture rising demand.

supporting_facts.fact: Search accounts for 30% "Share of Category Spend".
supporting_facts.relevance_to_recommendation: Supports prioritizing Search efficiency and budget allocation fixes now: if Search is 30% of category spend, it is a major battleground for retail growth. With the account constrained by budget and leaking into low-return queries, tightening controls and reallocating/adding budget can materially change outcomes in a channel that commands a large portion of spend.

supporting_facts.fact: Pilot Account (this report) is listed at 9.0% "Spend Share" and "Channels": "Search (primary)".
supporting_facts.relevance_to_recommendation: Highlights concentration risk and urgency: the account is comparatively smaller in spend share (9.0%) versus top competitors (e.g., 28%, 21%). With Search as the primary channel, remaining budget-capped (and carrying query waste) is especially costly—improving allocation and reducing leakage is the fastest path to defend and grow share.

email_copy.subject: USD 54,575 this quarter is getting left on the table by budget caps + query leakage
email_copy.hook: Your paid search account isn’t losing auctions because you’re getting out-positioned — it’s mostly getting throttled. The growth campaigns are basically running at the ceiling, while a meaningful chunk of exposure is slipping into competitor/low-intent queries that don’t pay you back.
why_now_bullets: Retail auctions are heating up: 9.0% Search Spend Growth QoQ in the US, while your account is still capped and can’t keep pace.
Demand is rising on the exact seasonal intent you’re already paying for: 21% growth on “winter jacket sale” (index 100 -> 121), but those high-intent terms are still losing visibility.
Right now the account is running at 21.29% impression share while the market benchmark sits at 35.0% — and you’re losing 78.7% of impression share to budget.
email_copy.stat_sub: At current demand levels, from removing caps + tightening control
email_copy.impact_line: Based on what your account is currently missing due to budget throttling (with USD 9,400/day already fully pressured in key campaigns) plus the preventable waste dragging Search efficiency, there’s a clear path to unlock USD 54,575 in incremental revenue this quarter without changing your entire strategy.
email_copy.scope_intro: Below is the campaign-by-campaign view of where that USD 54,575 is concentrated, so you can see exactly which areas deserve funding first — and which ones need guardrails before they’re allowed to scale.
email_copy.cards_intro: Here’s the short diagnosis and fix order: stop the competitor-term bleed, remove the self-inflicted blocks, then reallocate/raise budgets only where marginal returns justify it — with a targeted bid/structure pass to recover lost rank on high-QS seasonal terms.
email_copy.working_intro: Also worth calling out: the foundation is solid — you already have strong ad quality and competitive positioning, so these changes are about unlocking volume, not rebuilding from scratch.
email_copy.opportunity_intro: If you want a concrete payoff target: moving from 21.29% impression share toward 35.0% is where the incremental volume comes from — and it’s the cleanest route to capturing that USD 54,575 while competition and costs rise.
email_copy.fix_title: Want me to map this into a 14-day rollout (what to change first + what to watch)?
email_copy.fix_body: Reply with “Tue” or “Thu” and I’ll send two time options for a quick working session. If you’d rather keep it async, reply “Plan” and I’ll email the prioritized rollout in order of impact.
email_copy.ps: P.S. Notably, your account shows 0.0% lost to rank at the campaign level while still losing visibility at the keyword level — that’s usually a structural/segmentation issue, which is good news because it’s fixable fast.
